page: Amazon Web Services i3en.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance provides 8 vCPUs and 4 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz, with support for instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. Memory capacity is configured at 64 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, delivering 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage architecture features a bundled 5,000 GB local NVMe SSD, complemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network capability. No GPUs are attached.

Benchmark analysis reflects modest compute capabilities alongside steady I/O throughput. Geekbench single-core (1053.0) and multi-core (4039.0) scores, as well as stress-ng single-core performance (1284.28), fall into lower benchmark tiers. However, multi-core stress testing (6752.62) and PassMark CPU metrics (7704.22) achieve middle-tier results. Memory subsystem bandwidth maintains solid performance, recording 381.66 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 49.22 GB/sec for large un-cached blocks. In operational benchmarks, the instance delivers 6.48 million Redis SET operations per second and average database operation performance, while compute-bound tasks like compression and LLM token processing show weaker results.

The qualitative cost-efficiency profile of the i3en.2xlarge derives directly from its substantial NVMe storage density per vCPU. While compute-intensive tasks yield lower returns per resource unit due to older core throughput, operations requiring high local disk capacity and fast caching benefit significantly from the integrated high-speed storage without incurring external storage detachment latencies.

The instance is well suited for storage-heavy workloads, distributed file systems, data warehousing nodes, search index clusters, and large NoSQL or relational databases requiring local low-latency storage. It is less suitable for compute-intensive pipelines, heavy real-time compression, or large-scale AI inference workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services i3en.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance tailored for I/O-intensive workloads requiring large amounts of local storage. Powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, it features 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, paired with 64 GB of DDR4 memory. Its core architectural advantage is a bundled 5,000 GB local NVMe SSD and an 8 Gbps baseline network connection. Performance benchmarks demonstrate mid-range multi-threaded compute and solid database transaction rates, reaching 6.48 million Redis SET operations per second, though raw single-thread compute and compression speeds place in lower percentiles. The instance delivers high resource density for data-centric operations, making it suitable for distributed databases, caching clusters, and search engine nodes.
